title: 28 U.S.C. § 1367 — supplemental jurisdiction
summary: Supplemental jurisdiction allows a federal court with an authorized anchor claim to hear certain related claims that lack an independent federal jurisdictional basis. The statute imposes conditions, exclusions, and grounds for declining the additional claims.

sections.Role in the course: Supplemental jurisdiction allows a federal court with an authorized anchor claim to hear certain related claims that lack an independent federal jurisdictional basis. The statute imposes conditions, exclusions, and grounds for declining the additional claims.
sections.What to examine: First identify a claim within original federal jurisdiction. Ask whether the other claim belongs to the same Article III case or controversy. Then apply § 1367(b) where original jurisdiction rests solely on diversity, and § 1367(c)’s grounds for declining jurisdiction.
